title: Pre-Analysis — Self-Lubricating Bushes in the Cargo Door Latch Shaft Bearings
abstract: Closed pre-analysis of the grease-free latch shaft bushes, covering the temporary bracket repair already in service, the door warning content that reads the same latch sensors and the part list the line orders the bush kit from.

sections.objective: Confirm that a grease-free bush can be introduced into the cargo door latch shaft bearings without disturbing the latch rigging, the door warning logic or the repairs already carried out on the latch brackets, and decide what has to be re-issued at the same time. The work order was raised internally after operators in wet and de-icing environments reported latch stiffness that traced to washed-out lubricant, and was asked to report in time for the following production standard.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed and the temporary bracket repair was the one that mattered. A number of aircraft carry an impact damage repair on the latch bracket that was designed around the greased bush and its clearance, and the self-lubricating item runs a different fit at temperature. Fitting the new bush into a repaired bracket was shown to close the clearance below the rigging tolerance on the cold day case, so the repair had to be listed as an exclusion. The warning system content was the second theme: the proximity sensors are read by the door test and by the fault symptom procedure, and both quote the latch shaft functional item numbers, although neither needed a technical change.
sections.next_steps: List the temporary bracket repair as an exclusion in the bulletin effectivity and give the affected operators a permanent repair scheme before the campaign opens. Re-issue the illustrated part list with the new bush and the deleted grease fitting. Confirm with the door system owner that the sensor gap statement in the operational test still holds with the new bush at the low-temperature limit.

tasks.title: Search repairs and modifications on the latch mechanism
Check the rigging tolerance stack with the new bush fit
Review door warning content quoting the latch shaft items

expected_findings.rationale: The temporary impact damage repair on the latch bracket was designed around the greased bush and its running clearance. With the self-lubricating item the stack closes below the rigging tolerance on the cold day case, so a repaired bracket cannot take the new bush as it stands.
expected_findings.resolution: Repair listed as an exclusion in the bulletin effectivity, with a permanent bracket scheme offered to the affected operators before the campaign opens.

expected_findings.rationale: The latching figure lists both shaft items, the bearing and the grease fitting that the change deletes. It is also the list the line orders from, so leaving it unchanged would keep the greased bush flowing into stores after the cut-in.
expected_findings.resolution: Re-issued with the new bush, the deleted fitting and a pre-mod and post-mod item split.

expected_findings.rationale: The fault symptom procedure for a cargo door indication that stays on after closing works through latch travel and sensor gap, and quotes both latch shaft functional item numbers. Its most probable cause list names lubricant migration, which stops being a cause once the bush is grease-free.
expected_findings.resolution: Cause list re-ordered for post-mod aircraft; no change to the test steps.

expected_findings.rationale: The forward fuselage sheet carries the proximity sensor return for the same functional item in the door surround. Nothing electrical changes, but the sheet note names the bearing standard when describing the sensor bracket datum.
expected_findings.resolution: Sheet note corrected at the next routine revision; no wiring change.

type_data.conclusion: Validated with the repaired-bracket population excluded from the bulletin effectivity.
